rules.title: Well-child visits come fast in the first two years
rules.body: The AAP schedule sets about a dozen well-child visits between birth and age three, then one a year. Book the next one before you leave each appointment.

evidence.label: American Academy of Pediatrics
evidence.citation: AAP Recommendations for Preventive Pediatric Health Care (periodicity schedule), as of 2026-09

rules.title: Book this year's well-child visit
rules.body: From age three through the teen years the AAP recommends a well-child visit every year, and most insurance covers it in full. Slots near school breaks go first.

evidence.label: American Academy of Pediatrics
evidence.citation: AAP Recommendations for Preventive Pediatric Health Care (periodicity schedule), as of 2026-09

rules.title: Flu vaccine season is open
rules.body: The CDC recommends a flu vaccine for everyone 6 months and older, ideally by the end of October — pharmacies take walk-ins, and one trip covers the whole household.

evidence.label: CDC
evidence.citation: CDC seasonal influenza vaccination recommendations, as of 2026-09

rules.title: Preteen checkup: Tdap, HPV, and meningococcal vaccines
rules.body: Around the 11-12 birthday the CDC schedule adds the Tdap booster, the two-dose HPV series, and the first meningococcal shot — catch-up is possible at any age.

evidence.label: CDC
evidence.citation: CDC child and adolescent immunization schedule, as of 2026-09

rules.title: Age 16: meningococcal booster is due
rules.body: The CDC schedule calls for a MenACWY booster at 16, ahead of the years when meningococcal risk peaks. Some colleges require proof of it.

evidence.label: CDC
evidence.citation: CDC child and adolescent immunization schedule, as of 2026-09
